name: Book, allocate and enrich executed trades
summary: Trade support turns each executed order into booked trades in the investment book of record, split across the portfolios and custody accounts named on the order and enriched with settlement dates, standing settlement instructions and fees, ready for confirmation with the broker. Most trades flow from the order management system into SimCorp Dimension without anyone touching them; analysts work the exceptions, such as manual tickets for funding and OTC trades, allocations that do not divide cleanly, unknown securities, missing broker instructions and breaks between the order system and the book of record. Every manual booking, amendment and instruction change is checked by a second person, and breaks must be cleared the same day because errors here become confirmation mismatches and settlement fails later.

baseline.org_archetype: A very large Canadian national pension fund manager with an internal trading desk, an order and execution management system and SimCorp Dimension as its investment book of record.
baseline.notes: Volume follows the organisation file estimate of about 40,000 trade allocations a month. One order produces on average about 1.6 allocations (several portfolios or accounts, or several executing brokers).

trigger: An execution report for a completed order arrives from the OMS, or a trader's ticket arrives for a trade executed outside the OMS.
end_state: The allocation is booked, enriched and released to confirmation as a trade ticket, or cancelled as a duplicate or busted trade.

volume.seasonality: Follows trading volume: peaks in volatile markets, at quarter-ends and on index rebalancing dates; most allocations arrive after the North American close.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate (process mkt-book-allocate); timing of allocations after the close from t1report.

26 trade support analysts split between booking and allocation, confirmation and affirmation and OTC lifecycle events. Loaded cost from the organisation file; Job Bank NOC 11109 Toronto median is C$34.62 an hour before incentives, benefits and overhead.
Maker-checker approvals and SSI verification; 10 seniors share several processes.

roles.title: Director, middle office and trade support

evidence.note: Aged break escalations only.
Answering trade support queries on breaks.
Rare non-pro-rata allocation approvals.
New securities and accounts triggered by trades; most security setup happens in io-data-management ahead of trading.

systems.name: Order and execution management system with pre-trade compliance rules
SimCorp Dimension investment book of record (portfolio accounting, treasury, performance)
Bloomberg terminals, market data and trade messaging
DTCC Central Trade Manager trade matching
Cloud enterprise data platform and data warehouse

steps.name: Execution report or trade ticket arrives for booking
steps.description: When an order is done the OMS sends the execution report with average price, quantity, broker and the pre-allocation by portfolio and account. Credit trades from Credit Investments arrive the same way; funding trades, OTC derivatives and some voice trades arrive as tickets from the trader instead.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: electronic execution report from the OMS
manual ticket (funding, OTC derivative, voice or off-system trade)

evidence.note: Allocation is the first post-trade step and about 80% of institutional allocations happen after the close (t1report). The manual share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Key a manual trade ticket into the book of record
steps.description: A trade support analyst reads the trader's ticket, Bloomberg message or term sheet and keys the trade into SimCorp Dimension: instrument, counterparty, portfolio, quantity or notional, price, trade and settlement dates and fees.

error.defect_description: Keying error in counterparty, notional, price, dates or portfolio.

evidence.note: ISDA found 11% of interest rate derivative trade records contained errors in 2011, most from the front office, with counterparty name and payment dates the top causes (isda_obs). Touch time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Second person checks the manual ticket
steps.description: A senior associate compares the booked trade field by field with the source ticket or term sheet and approves it in SimCorp, or sends it back with the error marked.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Maker-checker on manual bookings: trades authorised and recorded accurately (SOC 1 baseline trading objective)

evidence.note: SOC 1 baseline objective that trades are properly authorised and recorded accurately (sifma_soc); return rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Apply the allocation across portfolios and accounts
steps.description: The OMS or SimCorp splits the block across the portfolios and custody accounts named on the order at the average price, pro rata for partial fills, and rounds to board lots or minimum bond denominations.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: rounding, minimum denomination or partial fill exception

evidence.note: Block orders allocated according to management methodologies (sifma_soc); blocks reviewed and allocated as soon as practicable (fxgc). Exception share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Resolve an allocation exception
steps.description: The analyst adjusts allocations that do not divide cleanly (odd lots, bond minimum denominations, a partial fill across several accounts), applying the desk's pro-rata rule, and records the reason.

error.defect_description: Allocation adjusted to the wrong account or quantity.

next.condition: proposed allocation departs from pro rata

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Approve a non-pro-rata allocation
steps.description: The head of the trading desk reviews why the allocation departs from pro rata (for example a mandate limit or a minimum holding) and approves or rejects it in writing.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Fair allocation policy: allocations follow the stated method and departures are approved by management (SOC 1 baseline allocation objective)

evidence.note: Allocations approved by management (sifma_soc).

steps.name: Interface loads allocations into SimCorp
steps.description: The interface between the OMS and SimCorp Dimension, the investment book of record, posts each allocation as a trade in the right portfolio. It runs in frequent intraday batches.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: rejected: unknown security, account or broker code

evidence.note: SimCorp is the book of record (fund_simcorp); the order-to-settlement chain was not yet one integrated platform (ar21). Rejection share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Investigate an interface rejection
steps.description: The analyst opens the interface error queue, reads the reject reason and checks whether the security, portfolio, account or broker code is missing or mapped wrongly in reference data.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: new security or account must be set up

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Set up the new security or account in reference data
steps.description: An investment data analyst creates the security master record from Bloomberg (identifiers, currency, conventions, pricing source, settlement market) or maps the new account, and a second person approves it before trades can load.

error.defect_description: Wrong convention, currency or settlement market on the new security.

control.basis: New securities and changes authorised and processed accurately (SOC 1 baseline objective); maker-checker on the security master

evidence.note: New security setup control objective (sifma_soc); stale reference data causes settlement errors (t1report).

steps.name: Enrich the trade with settlement details
steps.description: SimCorp adds the settlement date from the market calendar, the custody account, the place of settlement and the counterparty's standing settlement instructions, and calculates commissions, fees and transaction taxes.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: commission, fee or tax outside tolerance

evidence.note: Automated SSI enrichment from ALERT supports straight-through processing (dtcc_alert, dtcc_ctm). Exception shares are author estimates.

steps.name: Research a missing or conflicting SSI
steps.description: The analyst looks up the broker's instructions in ALERT and earlier emails, works out which instruction applies to the market and asset type and asks the broker to update ALERT or confirm the instruction in writing.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Outdated, incomplete or inaccurate SSI data is a leading cause of trade exceptions and settlement failure (dtcc_alert); missing or incorrect SSIs and customers not updating SSIs are named causes of settlement errors (t1report).

steps.name: Wait for the broker to supply the instruction
steps.description: The broker's operations team updates its ALERT record or sends the instruction on letterhead or authenticated message. Small or foreign brokers can take longer.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Verify and approve the SSI change
steps.description: A senior associate verifies the new instruction against an independent source (ALERT record or a call-back to a known contact), checks it was not changed by an email request alone, and approves it in the SSI table.

error.defect_description: Wrong instruction approved, causing a mismatch at the custodian.

control.basis: SSI changes verified independently and approved by a second person (payment fraud and settlement control); FX Global Code principle 51 on standard settlement instructions

evidence.note: Use of SSIs (fxgc principle 51) and accurate recording of trades (sifma_soc). Call-back practice is common anti-fraud control; time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Check commissions, fees and taxes
steps.description: The analyst compares the calculated commission with the broker's agreed rate and checks stamp duty, financial transaction tax or exchange fees for the market, then corrects the trade or asks the broker to correct its figures.

error.defect_description: Fee corrected on our side when the broker was wrong.

evidence.note: Author estimate; commission differences are a common matching exception in CTM.

steps.name: Hourly trade reconciliation of the OMS against SimCorp
steps.description: An automated control compares executions in the OMS with trades in SimCorp each hour and at end of day by quantity, price, portfolio and broker, and lists missing, duplicate or different trades.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Organisation file process description: breaks between the order system and the book of record are fixed the same day. Hourly cadence and break share are author estimates.

steps.name: Investigate a trade break
steps.description: The analyst compares the OMS execution, the SimCorp trade and the broker's execution summary to find which side is wrong (missing or duplicate trade, wrong portfolio, price, quantity or broker).

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

next.condition: trader must confirm the correct details
duplicate or busted trade cancelled with no rebooking

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Trader confirms the correct trade details
steps.description: The analyst messages the trader, who checks the execution in the EMS or with the broker and confirms the right price, quantity, broker or portfolio.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Amend or cancel and rebook the trade
steps.description: The analyst corrects the SimCorp trade, or cancels it and books it again, with a reason code so that the change is visible downstream to confirmation and settlement.

error.defect_description: Correction itself mistyped.

evidence.note: Cancel and rebill processes create inconsistencies and drive settlement errors (t1report).

steps.name: Second person approves the amendment
steps.description: A senior associate checks the amendment against the confirmed details and approves it, or rejects it back to the analyst.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Maker-checker on trade amendments and cancellations

next.condition: still unresolved at end of day

evidence.note: Trades recorded accurately and completely (sifma_soc).

steps.name: Escalate an aged break
steps.description: Breaks not cleared by end of day are reported to the director of trade support with the cause and owner, logged on the daily break report and chased first thing the next morning.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

control.basis: Investment operations break management standard: breaks cleared the same day or escalated

evidence.note: Author estimate based on the same-day break rule in the organisation file description.

steps.name: Release the booked trade ticket to confirmation
steps.description: The booked, allocated and enriched trade ticket becomes available to confirmation: SimCorp or the OMS sends the allocation to CTM for broker-matched trades, or queues it for FX and OTC confirmation.

error.defect_description: None introduced; earlier errors pass through.

evidence.note: Allocations go to the broker through CTM to start confirmation and affirmation (dtcc_ctm, dtcc_auto).

exceptions.name: Manual ticket
exceptions.description: Funding, OTC derivative and voice trades are keyed by hand and checked by a second person.

exceptions.name: Allocation exception
exceptions.description: Odd lots, bond minimum denominations or partial fills need manual adjustment; a few need desk-head approval for a non-pro-rata split.

exceptions.name: Unknown security or account
exceptions.description: The book of record rejects the trade until reference data sets up the new security or account.

exceptions.name: Missing or conflicting SSI
exceptions.description: The broker's settlement instruction is missing, out of date or ambiguous and must be obtained, verified and approved.

exceptions.name: OMS to book of record break
exceptions.description: A missing, duplicate or different trade is investigated, often with the trader, then amended under maker-checker; unresolved breaks are escalated at day end.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from execution report to trade ticket released to confirmation
benchmarks.population: Author estimate for a large buy-side middle office using an OMS feeding a book of record

evidence.note: Clean trades load and enrich within about an hour of the order completing; exceptions take hours and aged breaks run to the next morning. Allocation timing (80% after the close) from t1report.

benchmarks.population: U.S. institutional trades processed through DTCC, 2021

evidence.note: About 20% of allocations occur during the trading day and 80% after the close (DTCC internal analysis).

benchmarks.unit: share of interest rate derivative trade records

evidence.note: 18% in 2009, 14% in 2010, 11% in 2011; used to anchor the manual ticket error rate.

pain_points.description: Most allocations arrive after the close in a burst, so exceptions pile up in the evening just when broker operations teams are also busiest.

evidence.note: 80% of allocations after the close.

pain_points.description: Missing or stale broker settlement instructions stop straight-through processing and, if missed, cause settlement fails later.

evidence.note: Inaccurate SSI data is a leading cause of exceptions and fails.

pain_points.description: Manual re-keying of funding, OTC and unusual trades introduces errors that need a second person to check.

evidence.note: OTC trade record error rates (isda_obs); the integrated trading life cycle platform was still being built (ar21).

pain_points.description: Separate order and accounting systems create breaks that must be found and fixed the same day.

evidence.note: Investment Lifecycle Technology & Data project to integrate the public markets trade life cycle (ar21).

sources.title: The model fund F2021 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2021)

sources.title: The model fund Goes Live with SimCorp to Support Growth
sources.supports: SimCorp Dimension used for portfolio accounting, treasury and performance measurement after the fund internalised record keeping

sources.title: Accelerating the U.S. Securities Settlement Cycle to T+1
sources.supports: About 20% of institutional allocations occur during the trading day and 80% after the close; affirmation deadline 11:30 AM ET on T+1 under T+2; confirmation and affirmation can only start once allocations are complete; causes of settlement errors and fails include missing or incorrect SSIs, stale reference data, recalls and cancel and rebill

sources.title: Asset Manager's Guide to SOC 1
sources.publisher: SIFMA Asset Management Group and Grant Thornton
sources.supports: Baseline SOC 1 control objectives: trades properly authorised, settled and recorded accurately, completely and timely; block orders allocated according to management methodologies and allocations approved; new securities authorised and processed accurately; cash and positions reconciled to custodians

sources.title: FX Global Code (updated December 2024; first published 2017)
sources.supports: Principles 46 to 55: confirm trades as soon as practicable using automated matching; review, affirm and allocate block transactions as soon as practicable; resolve confirmation and settlement discrepancies; measure settlement risk and use PVP where practicable; use standard settlement instructions; request direct payments; reconcile accounts and submit compensation claims in a timely manner

sources.title: ALERT: standing settlement instruction platform
sources.supports: Industry's largest SSI database, shared automatically with counterparties; enrichment with CTM supports straight-through processing; 57% of ALERT SSIs managed by custodians and prime brokers; outdated, incomplete or inaccurate SSI data is a leading cause of trade exceptions and settlement failure

sources.title: Central Trade Manager (CTM)
sources.supports: Central matching platform automating allocation, confirmation and matching for equities, fixed income and money markets; Match to Instruct workflow with ALERT and TradeSuite ID; optional SSI enrichment; dashboards with same-day match agreed rates

sources.title: Why Automation is Pivotal to Prepare for T+1 in U.S.
sources.supports: Workflow of allocation, confirmation and affirmation; centrally matched trades can be affirmed and instructed automatically; affirmation deadline 11:30 AM ET on T+1; near 100% affirmation by 9 PM on trade date for automated workflows

sources.title: ISDA Operations Benchmarking Survey 2011
sources.supports: Interest rate derivative trade records containing errors 18% (2009), 14% (2010), 11% (2011), most attributable to the front office; counterparty name and payment dates are top error sources; 83% of electronically eligible interest rate derivative events confirmed electronically in 2011; confirmation backlogs measured in business days outstanding

sources.title: Wages: Credit Counsellor and other financial officers (NOC 11109) in the Toronto Region
sources.supports: Toronto Region hourly wages for NOC 11109: low 23.00, median 34.62, high 66.46 (2023-2024)

assumptions: The unit of work is one allocation (one portfolio or account's share of one broker execution); about 1.6 allocations per order is assumed to reconcile 25,000 orders with 40,000 allocations a month.
The OMS sends pre-allocated executions to SimCorp Dimension through an interface; SimCorp is the book of record and holds the SSI table, enriched from DTCC ALERT for brokers that use it.

Exception rates (6% manual tickets, 6% allocation exceptions, 3% SSI exceptions, 3% fee exceptions, 3% OMS to book of record breaks) are author estimates for a large buy-side middle office in 2019 to 2022.

Non-pro-rata allocation approval is given by the head of the trading desk (cmf_trading_director), a role not listed for this process in the organisation file; new security setup is done by the investment data team (data_ops_analyst), also not listed.
Trade support analysts and seniors also work on confirmation and affirmation and OTC lifecycle events, so their FTE here is a share of the team.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file; they include incentive pay and an overhead factor of 1.25.
